claims.title: Folding-fin mechanism model
claims.question: Can the specified four-bar linkage carry the fin from folded (0 deg) to 92 deg and hold it over-center?
claims.statement: In the planar model, the specified baseline linkage (ground 25, coupler 60, input 15, output 15 mm) cannot close at any drive angle from 0 to 92 deg, and none of the 81 swept variants can. Transmission-angle and envelope requirements therefore cannot be evaluated, and over-center locking is not modeled.
assumptions: The mechanism is a planar, pin-jointed four-bar loop.
Link lengths are pin-centre distances in millimetres.
The drive angle is measured from the folded position.
limitations: A planar model cannot tell whether a different topology or pivot layout was intended.
Loop geometry says nothing about loads, clearance, compliance, or locking torque.
Rendered or exported CAD of the links is not evidence that the mechanism assembles.
concerns: Which topology and dimensions were intended? The recorded dimensions cannot form a closed loop (D-002).
measurement_needed: Reviewer confirmation of the intended link dimensions and topology.
A revised, reviewed model; only then an inert, instrumented deployment test of a printed linkage.

claims.title: Deployment timing
claims.question: Does the hardware-timed deploy output fire at the requested delay with sub-millisecond jitter, without blocking the control loop?
claims.statement: Firmware schedules the deploy output with a one-shot esp_timer at a requested 50 ms delay. No hardware timing has been measured; the only timing data is a 21-row synthetic fixture that exercises report arithmetic.
assumptions: The requested delay in firmware is the intended deployment delay.
Jitter means the spread of output-edge time relative to the trigger, measured by an instrument independent of the ESP32 clock.
limitations: Synthetic values do not demonstrate timer, scheduler, or actuator behavior.
Twenty-one rows cannot bound a tail latency even if they were real.
The existing bench sketch times the callback with the clock it is measuring (D-024).
measurement_needed: Inert GPIO 33 edge timing against an external trigger reference, per proposed pre-registration P-001.
claims.status_meaning: An open question, conflict, or missing measurement blocks a stronger statement.

claims.title: Material mass accounting
claims.question: Does substituting CFRP and Ti-6Al-4V for the baseline materials reduce mass by 30-40%?
claims.statement: For the four parts listed in parts.yaml, substituting CFRP and Ti-6Al-4V for 7075-T6 reduces calculated mass by 36.0% (98.1 g to 62.8 g). No part has been weighed, the listed baseline is not the PLA/PETG prototype, and the listed fin volume is inconsistent with the fin mass used by C6 and C8.
assumptions: Part volumes, densities, and the four-part scope represent the assembly the claim is about.
limitations: Calculated differences are not measured savings.
Electronics, servos, fasteners, motor, and manufacturing variation are excluded.
The candidate materials have not been built.
concerns: The rollup's fin (about 5 g in CFRP) and the 154 g fin used by C6 and C8 cannot both describe the same design (D-010).
The 7075-T6 baseline is not the printed prototype (D-022).
measurement_needed: One reconciled design point shared by C4, C6, C7, and C8.
As-built part masses on a calibrated scale for whatever is actually built.

claims.title: Static-stability model
claims.question: Does the modeled rocket keep a static margin of 1.5-2.0 calibers through the motor burn?
claims.statement: The reference Barrowman script reports 1.55-1.57 cal during a hard-coded Estes C6-5 burn. An unreviewed textbook re-derivation of the fin terms, sharing every other input, gives 0.74-0.76 cal. The two disagree about the 1.5-2.0 cal window, and the script's motor differs from the OpenRocket model's AeroTech G64W.
assumptions: The OpenRocket file's geometry and override masses describe the intended rocket.
A Barrowman static margin is the quantity the 1.5-2.0 cal target refers to.
limitations: A static margin does not establish dynamic stability or flight readiness.
The fin geometry was revised to meet the target; matching a target is not validation (D-009).
Neither model has been independently reviewed.
concerns: Which fin-term formulation is correct for this geometry (D-006)?
Which motor should the CG history use (D-007)?
measurement_needed: Independent review of the Barrowman formulation and inputs.
An inert balance-point measurement of the assembled airframe's dry CG (compare to PRED-C5-DRY-CG).

claims.title: Spring margin consistency
claims.question: Does the stated 220 N*m/rad torsion spring exceed the calculated minimum rate by at least 20%?
claims.statement: At the stated design point the calculated minimum spring rate is 184.9 N*m/rad. The stated 220 N*m/rad spring gives a 19.0% margin, below the stated requirement of at least 20%. No spring has been characterized.
assumptions: The requirement and the reported margin use the same definition: (k_supplied - k_min) / k_min.
The design point (205 m/s, 120 mm chord, 154 g fin, 50 ms deployment) is the intended one.
limitations: The damping treatment divides by (1 - damping ratio), a heuristic.
Design-point inputs were revised to match the paper's k_min (D-009).
No component has been measured.
concerns: The calculated margin is below the stated requirement (D-011).
measurement_needed: A decision on the requirement or the spring, recorded by a human.
Inert torque-angle characterization of the supplied spring (proposed pre-registration P-002).

claims.title: Deployment reliability evidence
claims.question: Does simulated deployment succeed in at least 99.9% of trials under manufacturing tolerances, and is that simulation informative?
claims.statement: A seeded 10,000-trial deployment simulation records 10,000 successes, and the denominator is now explicit. The model cannot fail its velocity criterion for a locked trial and uses a different fin and speed than C6, so the 100% figure does not discriminate between designs. No physical deployment has been observed.
assumptions: A reliability statement needs a trial count, seed, model revision, and outcome definition.
limitations: Simulation outcomes do not measure physical reliability.
No empirical confidence bound is asserted.
The simulated fin, speed, and spring treatment differ from C6 (D-010, D-013).
concerns: The success criterion cannot fail for a locked trial, so the result cannot discriminate designs (D-013).
measurement_needed: A reviewed model whose failure modes can occur, run at the shared design point.
Repeated inert deployment trials of a physical mechanism once C1 is resolved.

claims.title: Structural claim boundaries
claims.question: Does the quasi-isotropic CFRP fin match or exceed aluminium stiffness, and does the Ti-6Al-4V hinge pin keep a factor of safety above 1.5?
claims.statement: Classical laminate theory gives Ex = 56.68 GPa for the quasi-isotropic layup, below the 69 GPa aluminium comparison, so the stiffness claim is not met on modulus. A closed-form hinge-pin check gives a factor of safety of 1.88 against a 1.5 threshold. Neither is a physical test.
assumptions: Handbook lamina properties, ideal layup, and the stated 50 g load case represent the design.
limitations: Material modulus and component bending stiffness are different quantities.
An analytical factor of safety is not a qualification test.
Manufacturing defects and actual loads are unmeasured.
The hinge load uses the 154 g fin whose mass conflicts with C4 (D-010).
concerns: The modulus result is below the comparison material (D-015); a thickness-compensation argument has not been calculated.
measurement_needed: A component bending-stiffness calculation for equal-mass sections, reviewed.
Coupon or component stiffness measurement if a CFRP fin is ever made.

discrepancies.title: The specified four-bar cannot be assembled

sides.says: Ground 25, coupler 60, input 15, output 15 mm deploys the fin 0-92 deg.

Over the 0-92 deg drive range the B-D distance never exceeds 29.6 mm (40 mm at any angle), but the coupler and output circles only meet at 45 mm or more; no pose closes. None of the 81 variants closes at any pose.

sides.says: transmission_angle() returned 90.0 for poses that cannot close; an empty trajectory produced an envelope of 0.0; the Freudenstein constants were misassigned.
Tests asserted 40-140 deg and a bounded envelope, and passed because the placeholders sat inside those bounds.

discrepancies.found_by: Comparing compute_theta4 with direct circle intersection for a linkage that does close.

preregistrations.title: Deploy-output timing on inert hardware
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: When the firmware requests a 50 ms deploy delay, when does GPIO 33 rise relative to the trigger, and how much does that vary?
preregistrations.prediction: Edge at 50,000 us after the trigger reference; the paper claims jitter below 1,000 us. No model predicts the spread.

measured: time from trigger-reference edge to GPIO 33 rising edge, per trial

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Report median, maximum absolute deviation from 50,000 us, and trial count. R-C2-JITTER is satisfied only if the maximum absolute deviation over at least 1,000 trials is below 1,000 us after subtracting the instrument's stated timing uncertainty. Fewer trials: report the observation, do not evaluate the requirement.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Logic analyzer or oscilloscope sampling at 1 MHz or faster on GPIO 33 and on a second GPIO toggled immediately before trigger_deployment_sequence(); both channels share the instrument's clock.
known_limitations: The trigger-reference toggle itself adds a small, unmeasured offset.
Bench conditions exclude flight vibration, temperature, and brownout.
preregistrations.safety: Inert only: nothing connected to GPIO 33 except the instrument; ignition servo mechanically disconnected; no energetic material present.

preregistrations.title: Torsion spring rate of the supplied spring
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: What is the torque-angle rate of the spring that would be installed, and does it match the 220 N*m/rad in the claim?

measured: torque at each angle, loading and unloading

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Fit torque against angle over the rated range; report slope with its standard error and the hysteresis. Compare with 220 N*m/rad; the acceptance tolerance must be written here by the registering human before testing.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Static torque-angle fixture with a calibrated torque gauge or load cell at a known lever arm.
known_limitations: Static rate only; dynamic and temperature effects are not captured.
preregistrations.safety: Stored-energy hazard: restrain the spring, wear eye protection, release slowly.

preregistrations.title: Stationary roll-estimate drift
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: How far does the firmware roll estimate drift over 10 minutes with the rocket stationary and level, after CALIBRATE?
preregistrations.prediction: None. This is an exploratory characterization; no model predicts the drift.

measured: roll_deg from LOG rows (rocket clock) over 600 s
recorded: whether CALIBRATE was sent and when

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Report the roll change over 600 s and the maximum excursion. Because no prediction exists, the result describes this unit only and sets a baseline; it cannot pass or fail.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Dashboard session with DUMPLOG every 10 s to capture rocket-clock LOG rows; audit with python -m evidence audit.
known_limitations: The ring buffer holds about 12 s; missed dumps leave gaps that must be reported, not interpolated.
preregistrations.safety: Inert only: ignition servo disconnected; launcher left in SAFE.

specification.label: SPECIFICATION
specification.meaning: Authored requirement, boundary, note, or historical claim. States intent; demonstrates nothing.

implementation.label: IMPLEMENTATION
implementation.meaning: Source code, CAD source, model input, or configuration. Shows what was built, not how it behaves.

test_procedure.label: TEST PROCEDURE
test_procedure.meaning: Automated test source. A procedure, not a record that it ran or passed.

synthetic.label: SYNTHETIC
synthetic.meaning: Fabricated data that exercises tooling. Can never support a physical or performance claim.

analytical.label: ANALYTICAL
analytical.meaning: Output of a deterministic calculation. Only as good as its formulation and inputs.

simulated.label: SIMULATED
simulated.meaning: Output of a numerical or stochastic simulation. Not an observation of hardware.

execution_record.label: SOFTWARE VERIFIED
execution_record.meaning: A recorded run of automated checks. Shows software checks ran and passed, not that hardware works.

bench_observed.label: BENCH OBSERVED
bench_observed.meaning: Inert physical observation without a calibrated instrument (photo, video, operator log).

bench_measured.label: BENCH MEASURED
bench_measured.meaning: Inert physical measurement with a named instrument, method, and uncertainty.

open: An open question, conflict, or missing measurement blocks a stronger statement.
contradicted: Current evidence contradicts the claim or one of its requirements.
supported_within_limits: Evidence supports the statement as worded, at its evidence class only.
superseded: Replaced by another claim; retained for history.

principles: If the repository says it happened, point to the artifact.
A model is not a measurement.
A clean dataset is not proof of a physical event.
A passing test is not a qualification result.
Unknown is not zero. Missing is not false. Unmeasured is not passed.
Unresolved is a valid engineering state.
The claim works for the evidence, not the other way round.
ai_boundary: Automated tools, including AI assistants, may summarize, compare, explain, and propose.
They may not create measurements, relabel synthetic data as physical, edit raw evidence, fill missing records, register a pre-registration, accept a session, or record a human review.
They have no authority over arming, ignition, launch, or any safety gate.
Confidence is not authority: only a recorded inert measurement accepted by a named human enters the record.
limitations: Artifact presence and hash integrity are not scientific validation.
Evidence classes, claim statuses, assumptions, and discrepancies are authored declarations checked for internal consistency.
This build evaluates recorded values; it does not run models, tests, firmware, or hardware unless run records are attached.
A digest detects change against a trusted reference; it is not a signature.
No flight readiness, certification, or agency endorsement is asserted.

safety_gates.behavior: Leaving SAFE requires the switch; releasing it from any other state aborts to SAFE.
Launcher enters READY only after the rocket reports READY within 8 s; otherwise it aborts.
READY aborts if rocket telemetry stops for 2 s.
UDP launch is rejected with CMD_REJECT:dashboard_launch_disabled unless firmware is rebuilt with the opt-in.
Even with the opt-in, UDP launch is accepted only in READY.
Commands are ignored unless they come from the address that sent the shared-token HELLO.
The launch button must be held for 1 s with the switch still armed.

safety_gates.gate: Rocket ARM requires IDLE and a healthy IMU
safety_gates.behavior: ARM is refused (and now reported) otherwise.

safety_gates.gate: Rocket IGNITE requires ARMED and a healthy IMU
safety_gates.behavior: IGNITE is refused (and now reported) otherwise.

safety_gates.gate: Rocket IGNITE requires the deploy flag
safety_gates.behavior: IGNITE is refused unless the deploy timer has fired; see discrepancy D-017 for the ordering question.

safety_gates.gate: Deploy trigger requires a non-IDLE state
safety_gates.behavior: Handling an unarmed rocket cannot fire the deploy output.
IGNITE_FORCE exists only when BENCH_MODE is defined; the committed build does not define it.
Rocket refusals travel over UART as CMD_REJECT lines; the launcher forwards them and its own ABORT reasons to the dashboard CSV.
PID values outside 0-10 or malformed are rejected on both boards.

kinds.claim_vs_artifact: What a claim or note says differs from what its artifact contains.
kinds.requirement_vs_model: A model result does not meet a stated requirement.
kinds.model_vs_model: Two models of the same quantity disagree.
kinds.model_vs_input: A model's inputs differ from the design source it claims to use.
kinds.model_tuned_to_target: Model inputs were revised until a target was met.
kinds.implementation_defect: Software produced values that do not follow from its inputs.
kinds.test_vs_requirement: A test does not check what its name or claim says.
kinds.documentation_vs_implementation: Documentation disagrees with firmware or software behavior.
kinds.design_logic: Two implemented rules cannot both be satisfied in the intended sequence.
kinds.simulation_vs_cad: Simulation or model geometry disagrees with CAD geometry.
kinds.telemetry_vs_expected: Recorded telemetry disagrees with its documented meaning or rate.
kinds.bom_vs_design: The bill of materials disagrees with the design or firmware.
kinds.predicted_vs_measured: A physical measurement disagrees with its registered prediction.
kinds.provenance_gap: An artifact cannot be traced to the model revision that produced it.
kinds.measurement_method: A measurement procedure cannot establish what it is meant to measure.
